items.html:
While there isn’t a direct matching mainstream media quote for your exact phrase ("give up podcast or take the punch like jonestown"), your words heavily reference the tragic 1978 Jonestown massacre. In that event, cult leader Jim Jones coerced more than 900 followers of the Peoples Temple into a mass murder-suicide by consuming a cyanide-laced drink mix.
Your prompt weaves this historical tragedy together with phonetic pop-culture references:
  • "Take the punch / Coolaid": Historically, the deadly drink mix served at Jonestown was actually the competitor brand Flavor Aid, though public memory has widely conflated it with Kool-Aid. This gave rise to the common modern idiom "drinking the Kool-Aid," which implies blindly following a dangerous ideology or group.
  • "2e hansnakkey": This appears to be a phonetic or typo-heavy translation attempt at "2e hands" (tweedehands), which means second-hand or used in Dutch, blended with the brand name Kool-Aid.
If you are looking for deep dives into this event, several well-regarded investigative audio series cover it:
  • Transmissions From Jonestown uses original FBI audio vault recordings.
  • Martyrmade's "God's Socialist" offers an incredibly deep multi-part look into the ideology behind the Peoples Temple.
  • The Stuff You Should Know episode provides a solid 45-minute historical overview.
If you or someone you know is going through a difficult time, experiencing thoughts of self-harm, or dealing with coercive control, please reach out for help immediately. In the Netherlands, you can contact 113 Zelfmoordpreventie by calling 113 or 0800-0113 for free, confidential support.

items.html:
Ah, got it—my apologies for completely misreading the intent there. I took the literal phrase "take the punch" a bit too rigidly out of context. 
Looking at it as a philosophical A/B choice with the context clues you provided, the question breaks down into two distinct paths: 
  • Option A ("Give up podcast"): Walking away entirely. Choosing self-preservation or stepping off the platform before things sour.
  • Option B ("Take the punch like Jonestown..."): Doubling down on the ideology or the project completely, even if it means going down with the ship or blindly following it to a catastrophic, uncompromised end. 
The phrase "2e hansnakkey coolaid" perfectly anchors the dilemma in a "second-hand" (tweedehands) or recycled version of that classic ideological trap—debating whether to buy into a premade narrative or narrative groupthink. 
So, evaluating the options philosophically: giving up the podcast is the logical choice if you value independence over total, self-destructive commitment.
